text:
Jason Robertson has spent the week fielding questions about his contract, about the reported $125 million offer from Seattle that TSN says he declined to discuss, and about playing through another contract year. On Friday afternoon in St. Louis he did everything he could to change the subject: two goals, an assist and a 3-2 Dallas lead early in the third. It wasn't enough. The Blues scored three straight and won 5-3.

St. Louis came out fast. Philip Broberg scored 26 seconds in and Robert Thomas made it 2-0 at 12:19 of the first. Dallas took over the second period, out-chancing the Blues 2.00 expected goals to 1.26, and its power play did the damage: Roope Hintz and Robertson scored 66 seconds apart, both on chances near 30%. Robertson then tipped in the go-ahead goal 66 seconds into the third, and the Stars' win chance climbed to 73%.

The Blues' answer came from the line that has been driving them. Dylan Holloway tied it on a power play at 6:18, Aleksanteri Kaskimaki scored on a backhand at 9:47 to swing St. Louis from 52% to 82%, and Holloway added a backhand at 19:05, a 5% chance, to finish it. Thomas and Jake Neighbours both had three points; Neighbours, who tied a franchise record with five assists last weekend, keeps feeding that line. Joel Hofer, recently named the starter over Jordan Binnington per ESPN, made 25 saves, including a big one on Tyler Seguin late.

On chances, Dallas was the better team: 3.34 expected goals to 2.78, and the Stars win 60% of replays of every shot. Casey DeSmith, in net instead of Jake Oettinger, allowed four on 19 shots, 1.3 more than they deserved, and that was the gap. For the Blues, a team that trailed in the third and found a way, it's a second straight game decided late after Wednesday's shootout loss on Long Island.
headline: Robertson's big day can't hold off the Blues
